did_you_know.text: In this verse, the LORD describes His love for Zion as “a great zeal” and even “a great wrath”—expressing the intensity of His commitment to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is given two meaningful names: “the City of Truth” and “the Mountain of the LORD of hosts—the Holy Mountain.” Thus, the city is portrayed as a place of truth and holiness.
The vision of restoration includes security and long life: elderly men and women will sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of their advanced age.
Another sign of peaceful life in Jerusalem will be streets filled with boys and girls playing in them.
The LORD says that this promise may seem extraordinary to the remnant of the people, but He adds that it is not impossible in His eyes either.
The promise includes gathering the people from the lands of the east and from the land of the setting sun—in other words, from distant lands in both directions.
The purpose of returning to Jerusalem is not merely to live in the city: the people will be the LORD’s people, and He will be their God “in truth and in righteousness.”
The people are called to be strong while rebuilding the Temple, and the verse recalls the words of the prophets spoken on the day when the foundation of the LORD’s house was laid.
The social reform required of the people includes speaking the truth, carrying out judgments that promote peace at the city gates, and maintaining fair relationships with one another.

The four fasts—the fast of the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, and the tenth month—will become occasions of joy, gladness, and cheerful festivals. Alongside this change, the people are commanded to love truth and peace.
